Stand tall with your arms out to the sides.
Make controlled circles forward, then backward, keeping your shoulders relaxed.

Front-to-back leg swings. ten each leg.
Stand beside a wall with one hand supporting you.
Swing one leg forward and backward without arching your back.
Finish the prescribed reps or time, then switch legs.
Next is Front-to-back leg swings.

High knees on the spot. twenty seconds, light and quiet.
Stand tall and alternate lifting your knees in front of you, driving the opposite arm.

Lateral lunge. five each side.
Step out to one side and sit your hips back over the bent knee.
Keep the other leg long and both feet on the floor.
Push back to standing and repeat on the other side.
Next is Lateral lunge.
Back to Lateral lunge.
Standing hip controlled joint circles. three circles each leg each way.
Hold a wall and stand tall without twisting your torso.
Lift one knee, open it out, rotate it back and lower slowly.
Circle in both directions, then switch legs.
Next is Standing hip controlled joint circles.
Back to Standing hip controlled joint circles.
Lunge with twist. five each side.
Step into a lunge and turn your chest toward the front knee.
Return to standing and repeat on the other side, keeping the movement controlled.
Next is Lunge with twist.
Back to Lunge with twist.
Pogo hops. one set of ten reps, very low.
Stand tall, feet hip-width, hands on hips, on a mat.
Bounce on the balls of your feet with almost straight knees.
Let your heels touch the floor lightly.
Keep each bounce quick, quiet and springy.
Build height later.
Set one of one. ten reps.
Next is Pogo hops.
Back to Pogo hops.
For less noise, do fast heel raises without leaving the floor.
Single-leg balance. two sets of twenty seconds each leg, hand near a wall.
Stop the clock when the foot shifts, a hand leaves the hip or the raised foot touches down.
Stand on one leg next to a wall, hands on hips, other foot off the floor.
Hold for the time your level prescribes, then progress to eyes closed.
Once a month, record your best eyes-closed time per leg.
Set one of two. twenty seconds each leg.
Set two of two. twenty seconds each leg.
Next is Single-leg balance.
Back to Single-leg balance.
First side.
Change sides. Get into position for the other side.
Other side.
Heels-elevated goblet squat, slant-board squat. two sets of eight reps at the weight shown on screen, down to a chair, three seconds down.
Heels on a slant board or on two small plates or books, feet hip-width.
Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest.
Sit straight down to full depth with your torso upright.
Let your knees travel well past your toes.
Lower over three seconds, then push up to standing.
Set one of two. eight reps.
Set two of two. eight reps.
Strength is next.
Leave five or more easy reps in reserve.
Next is Heels-elevated goblet squat, slant-board squat.
Back to Heels-elevated goblet squat, slant-board squat.
Push-ups. two sets of six to eight reps, hands on a table or a wall.
Hands under the shoulders, body in one line, squeeze glutes and abs, .
Elbows about forty five degrees from the body.
Lower until the chest is a fist above the floor, then press to full lockout.
Too hard: hands on a sofa or bench.
Too easy: three seconds down, or feet raised.
Set one of two. six to eight reps.
Set two of two. six to eight reps.
Next is Push-ups.
Back to Push-ups.
One-arm dumbbell row. two sets of ten reps each side at the weight shown on screen.
Rest one hand and one knee on a chair or bed.
Keep your back flat and let the dumbbell hang.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, elbow close to the body.
Squeeze for one seconds, then lower to a full stretch.
Keep your torso still.
Set one of two. ten reps each side.
Set two of two. ten reps each side.
Next is One-arm dumbbell row.
Back to One-arm dumbbell row.
Poliquin step-up. one set of eight reps each leg, slant board on floor.
Start on a slant board on the floor, working heel elevated, with the other leg reaching forward.
The board alone gives a small heel tap, do not balance a large board on a narrow aerobic step.
Lower the other heel slowly to the floor in front by bending the working knee far over the toes.
Tap the heel lightly, then straighten the working knee to come up.
Hips level, don’t push off the floor leg.
Set one of one. eight reps each leg.
Next is Poliquin step-up.
Back to Poliquin step-up.
Two-leg tibialis raise. one set of twelve to fifteen reps.
Lean your back and hips on a wall with your feet thirty to sixty centimeters forward.
Keep both heels down and lift both sets of toes.
Pause for a second and lower slowly.
Set one of one. twelve to fifteen reps.
Core & knees is next.
Next is Two-leg tibialis raise.
Back to Two-leg tibialis raise.
Seated dumbbell calf raise. one set of twelve reps at two weights at the weight shown on screen.
Sit on a chair with the balls of your feet on a book or plate and dumbbells on your knees.
Raise your heels, pause, then lower into a comfortable stretch.
Set one of one. twelve reps.
Next is Seated dumbbell calf raise.
Back to Seated dumbbell calf raise.
Plank. two sets of fifteen to twenty seconds, knees down is fine.
Forearms on the floor, elbows under the shoulders.
Body straight, squeeze the glutes and brace the abs.
Look at the floor and breathe normally.
Set one of two. fifteen to twenty seconds.
Set two of two. fifteen to twenty seconds.
Next is Plank.
Back to Plank.
Hanging knee raise. two sets of five reps knee raises, small range.
Hang with your shoulders drawn slightly down.
Bring your bent knees toward your chest and curl your pelvis upward.
Lower slowly without swinging.
Set one of two. five reps.
Set two of two. five reps.
Next is Hanging knee raise.
Back to Hanging knee raise.
Lying leg raises on the floor.

Heart rate your prescribed heart-rate range, sixty to seventy percent of max, .
You can speak in full sentences.
Main indoor option: continuous step-ups on a stable low aerobic step, switching the lead leg every minute.
March instead if stepping raises your effort too much.
Mix in brisk marching with arm swings or side steps.
A skipping rope is an optional home alternative only while you can still talk comfortably, slow down or march if it pushes you above Zone two.
Music, a podcast or a series helps, Bryan rotates music, books and podcasts too.
Zone two is next.

Kneel with your back knee against a sofa or wall, shin running up it.
Other foot forward in a lunge.
Squeeze the back glute and tuck the pelvis, stay upright.
Cool-down is next.
Next is Couch stretch.
Back to Couch stretch.

Kneeling shin stretch. twenty to thirty seconds.
Kneel with the tops of your feet flat on the mat.
Sit back toward your heels.
For more stretch, lift the knees slightly with your hands.
Next is Kneeling shin stretch.
Back to Kneeling shin stretch.
Short intervals, twenty seconds bursts. four by, twenty seconds brisk, forty seconds easy.
Pick one or two moves from “Indoor interval moves”.
Work hard for twenty seconds, then march gently during the rest.

keep the pace brisk and below all-out effort.

Floor back extension. one set of ten reps, two seconds hold at top.
Lie face down, hands lightly at your temples or arms along your sides.
Squeeze your glutes, then lift your chest a few centimetres.
Hold one to two seconds and lower slowly.
Look at the floor so the neck stays long.
Back & core is next.
Next is Floor back extension.
Back to Floor back extension.
Dumbbell side bend. one set of ten reps each side at the weight shown on screen.
One dumbbell in one hand, the other hand on your waist.
Bend straight to the side, without twisting or leaning forward.
Squeeze the opposite side to return upright.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
Set one of one. ten reps each side.
Next is Dumbbell side bend.
Back to Dumbbell side bend.
Band Pallof press. two sets of six reps each side, two seconds hold.
Anchor a band at chest height on the hinge side of a closed door, stand side-on, a step away.
Hold the band at your sternum with both hands, knees soft.
Press the hands straight out and hold two seconds without letting the band turn you.
Bring your hands back slowly.
Do the same number of reps on both sides.
Set one of two. six reps each side.
Set two of two. six reps each side.
Next is Band Pallof press.
Back to Band Pallof press.
Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch. thirty seconds each side.
Half-kneel with the back knee on a cushion.
Tuck the pelvis and squeeze the back glute first.
Shift forward slightly and reach the same-side arm up.
Next is Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch.
Back to Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch.
Hamstring stretch. thirty seconds each side.
Rest your heel on a step or chair with your leg straight and toes up.
Hinge forward with a flat back until you feel the stretch.
Next is Hamstring stretch.
Back to Hamstring stretch.
Backward walk. two minutes.

Arm circles. one minutes, forward then backward.
Standing hip controlled joint circles. one minutes, both legs and directions.
Wall slides. one set of eight reps.
Head, upper back and buttocks on a wall, feet a small step out.
Forearms on the wall in a W shape.
Slide the arms up into a Y keeping contact, then pull the elbows down toward the ribs.
Slow reps, ribs stay down.
Set one of one. eight reps.
Next is Wall slides.
Back to Wall slides.
Thread the needle. five each side.
Start on your hands and knees.
Reach one arm under your body to the opposite side, shoulder toward the floor.
Then open it up to the ceiling, eyes following the hand.
Next is Thread the needle.
Back to Thread the needle.
Passive dead hang. three sets of ten to twenty seconds dead hang.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and let your body hang without swinging.
Relax your shoulders and breathe steadily for the prescribed time.
Support some of your weight with your feet when prescribed.
Set one of three. ten to twenty seconds.
Set two of three. ten to twenty seconds.
Set three of three. ten to twenty seconds.
Next is Passive dead hang.
Back to Passive dead hang.
Keep your toes lightly resting on the floor or a step to support twenty to thirty percent of your body weight.
A T G split squat. two sets of five reps each leg, part range, hand on a chair.
Long split stance, front foot flat, back knee on a cushion to start.
Slide forward until your hamstring covers your calf and the front knee is well past the toes, front heel stays down.
Keep the back leg long to stretch the hip flexor.
Keep a chair beside you for balance at first, add dumbbells later.
The animation shows the hands-free version.
Set one of two. five reps each leg.
Set two of two. five reps each leg.
Next is A T G split squat.
Back to A T G split squat.
Reverse Nordic. one set of five reps, small range.
Kneel upright on a mat, knees hip-width.
Squeeze the glutes so you form one straight line from knees to head.
Lean back as far as you can control, then return.
Start with a small range of motion and increase it each week.
Set one of one. five reps.
Next is Reverse Nordic.
Back to Reverse Nordic.
Overhead dumbbell triceps extension. one set of twelve reps at the weight shown on screen.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands overhead, elbows pointing forward.
Lower it behind your head, upper arms still.
Extend fully and hold one seconds at the top.
Ribs down, don’t arch the lower back.
Next is Overhead dumbbell triceps extension.
Back to Overhead dumbbell triceps extension.
Dumbbell biceps curl. one set of ten reps at the weight shown on screen.
Stand tall, elbows pinned at your sides.
Curl up while turning the palms up, squeeze at the top.
Lower over two to three seconds and keep your body still.
Next is Dumbbell biceps curl.
Back to Dumbbell biceps curl.
Band butterfly. one set of twelve reps, light band.
Anchor a band at chest height behind you, door hinge side, or wrap it around your upper back.
Arms out, elbows slightly bent.
Bring the hands together in front of the chest as if hugging a tree, squeeze one seconds.
Return slowly.
Next is Band butterfly.
Back to Band butterfly.
Farmer’seconds carry. two sets of twenty seconds at two weights at the weight shown on screen.
Hold a heavy dumbbell in each hand and stand tall using the string cue.
Keep your shoulders down and back.
Walk around the room with slow, steady steps for thirty to forty seconds.
Don’t let the dumbbells bang your legs or the shoulders roll forward.
Set one of two. twenty seconds.
Set two of two. twenty seconds.

Back to Farmer’seconds carry.
Cat-cow. ten breaths.
On hands and knees, hands under the shoulders.
Breathe out: round the back, tuck chin and tailbone.
Breathe in slowly as you lift your chest and tailbone.

Tree pose. two sets of twenty seconds each side, hand near a wall.
Stand on one leg, place the other foot on the inner calf or thigh, never on the knee.
Hands at the chest or overhead, fix your gaze on one point.

Set two of two. twenty seconds each side.
Next is Tree pose.
Back to Tree pose.
Cobra. three sets of ten seconds.
Lie face down, hands under the shoulders, elbows in.
Press up to lift the chest, hips stay on the floor.
Keep your neck long and look forward and down.

Single-leg toe touch. two sets of five reps each leg, hand on a wall, small range.
Stand on one leg, knee soft, other leg straight behind you with the toe just off the floor.
Hinge forward, reaching the opposite hand toward the standing foot, the back leg rises as a counterweight.
Hips stay square to the floor.
Stand back up by squeezing the glute.
Keep a wall within reach at first, the animation shows the hands-free version.

Bird dog. two sets of five reps each side, two seconds hold.
On hands and knees, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, back flat.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with the body.
Hold for two seconds without tilting your hips, then return and switch sides.
Set one of two. five reps each side.
Set two of two. five reps each side.
Next is Bird dog.
Back to Bird dog.
Dead bug. two sets of five reps each side.
Lie on your back, arms pointing at the ceiling, hips and knees bent at ninety degrees.
Press the lower back gently into the floor and keep it there.
Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor, then return.
Alternate sides, move slowly and breathe out as you extend.
Next is Dead bug.
Back to Dead bug.
Plank shoulder taps. two sets of six reps each side, from the knees.
High plank, hands under the shoulders, feet a bit wider than the hips.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder without the hips rocking.
Alternate slowly.
Wider feet make it easier.

Heidens, skater bounds. two sets of four reps each side, step and stick, no hop.
Stand on your right leg, knee slightly bent.
Bound sideways to the left and land on the left leg only.
Stick the landing for one to two seconds: hips back, knee over the toes.
Bound back.
Build distance before adding speed.
Set one of two. four reps each side.
Set two of two. four reps each side.

Rotational power: band woodchop. two sets of six reps each side, slow.
Anchor a band high on the hinge side of a closed door, stand side-on, an arm’seconds length away.
Grab with both hands, arms long, and pull diagonally down across your body to the opposite hip.
Turn from your hips and pivot your back foot.
Let the turn drive the movement through your arms.
Pull down quickly, then return over two to three seconds.
Next is Rotational power: band woodchop.
Back to Rotational power: band woodchop.
At easier levels, move slowly until you learn the movement.
Dumbbell Romanian deadlift. two sets of eight reps at two weights at the weight shown on screen.
Stop at a strong hamstring stretch, around mid-shin.
Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs with your knees slightly bent.
Push the hips back with a flat back, dumbbells sliding close to the legs.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall.
Next is Dumbbell Romanian deadlift.
Back to Dumbbell Romanian deadlift.
Reverse lunge. two sets of six reps each leg, hand on a chair.
Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides, bodyweight first, .
Step one foot back and lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Front knee may travel over the toes, torso tall.
Push through the front foot to return.
Alternate legs or finish one side first.
Set one of two. six reps each leg.
Set two of two. six reps each leg.
Next is Reverse lunge.
Back to Reverse lunge.
Dumbbell floor press. two sets of eight reps at two weights at the weight shown on screen.
Lie on your back, knees bent, a dumbbell in each hand beside your chest.
Press up until the arms are straight, lower until the upper arms touch the floor lightly.
Pause on the floor for one seconds without bouncing.
Next is Dumbbell floor press.

Stand tall, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing each other, elbows slightly forward.
Brace abs and glutes, press straight up until the arms are straight.
Head moves slightly back to let the dumbbells pass, then forward under them.
Lower in two seconds.
Don’t lean back.

Use a stable aerobic step or stair, starting at its lowest secure height.
A low step is the home adaptation of Bryan’seconds step-up.
Place your whole foot on the step.
Push through that leg until you stand tall.
Don’t push off the back foot.
Lower slowly.
Drive up under control, do not jump onto an aerobic step or stack loose risers or furniture.
Next is Bodyweight low step-up.
Back to Bodyweight low step-up.

On one forearm, elbow under the shoulder, feet stacked, bend your knees if that feels easier, .
Lift the hips into a straight line and hold.

Jefferson curl. two sets of five reps, no weight, on the floor, small range.
Stand on a step, legs straight, with a light weight, none at New to training, .
Tuck your chin and roll down one vertebra at a time toward your toes.
Hang two to three seconds, then roll up from the bottom, head last.
Move slowly and keep the weight light.
Do not try to lift heavy on this exercise.
Next is Jefferson curl.
Back to Jefferson curl.
Single-leg calf raise. one set of eight reps each leg, hand on a wall.
Stand on one foot on a stable step, holding a wall.
Raise your heel over two seconds, then lower over two seconds through a comfortable range.

Butterfly stretch, cobbler’seconds pose. thirty seconds.

String reset. thirty seconds.
Stand or sit with the feet grounded.
Imagine the string lifting the crown of your head: chin level, neck long.
Let the shoulders settle down and back without forcing them.
Take three slow breaths.
Repeat every time you sit down at your desk.
Posture correction is next.

Chin tucks. one set of six reps, three seconds hold.
Sit or stand tall, eyes level.
Glide your head straight back, making a slight double chin.
Don’t nod down.
Hold three seconds, release slowly.
Set one of one. six reps.

Back to Chin tucks.
Wall slides. one set of eight reps slow.
Band pull-apart. one set of twelve reps, lightest band.
Hold a light band at shoulder height, arms straight, hands shoulder-width.
Pull the band apart at chest height by squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Shoulders stay down, away from the ears, pause one seconds.
Next is Band pull-apart.
Back to Band pull-apart.
Band face pull. one set of twelve reps, lightest band.
Anchor the band at face height on the hinge side of a closed door.
Pull toward your eyes with elbows high and hands splitting apart.
Finish with thumbs pointing back and shoulder blades squeezed, hold one seconds.
Return slowly and stay tall.
Next is Band face pull.
Back to Band face pull.
External rotation with elbow on knee. one set of ten reps each arm at the weight shown on screen.
Stand with one foot on a stable chair and rest the working elbow on the inside of that knee, bent ninety degrees.
Hold a light dumbbell and rotate the forearm upward without moving the elbow.
Lower over two to three seconds, keeping the shoulder blade back and down.

Forehead resistance hold. three sets of ten seconds holds.
Bryan calls this technical and was taught it for his own diagnosed condition.
Stay gentle, and stop if you get dizziness, tingling or a headache.
Use thirty to fifty percent effort for the prescribed holds.
Stop for dizziness, tingling or a headache.
Sit or stand tall with your chin slightly tucked.
Place a hand on your forehead and resist gentle backward pressure without moving your head.

Doorway chest stretch. thirty seconds each side.
Keep your ribs down without arching your lower back.
Stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder.
Forearms on the door frame, elbows at shoulder height and bent ninety degrees.
Step one foot through and lean gently until you feel the stretch across the chest.
Next is Doorway chest stretch.
Back to Doorway chest stretch.
Shoulders up and out, levator shrug. one set of ten reps at two weights at the weight shown on screen, stop well before fatigue.
Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand, neck long, shoulders set back and down first.
Bend the elbows slightly and keep them pulled back, slightly behind the body.
Lift the shoulders up and out in a small arc, toward the ears and slightly forward.
Pause for one seconds at the top, then lower slowly.
Start light while you learn it, Bryan says the technique took him time.
Next is Shoulders up and out, levator shrug.
Back to Shoulders up and out, levator shrug.

Next is Slow forehead resistance.
Back to Slow forehead resistance.
Heel drops. one set of twenty reps drops.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart on a firm surface or thin mat.
Rise smoothly onto the balls of your feet, lifting heels three to five centimeters.
Drop your full body weight firmly down onto your heels with knees slightly soft, do not lock them, .
Feel the mechanical vibration pulse up through the shins, femur neck and lumbar spine.
Perform rhythmic, controlled drops: twenty to thirty reps for beginners, up to fifty for trained.
Set one of one. twenty reps.
Bone density protocol is next.
Next is Heel drops.

Stop the set if your landings get loud.
Rise onto your toes with your arms overhead.
Drop quickly into a quarter squat with your arms back.
Keep your feet on the floor.
Hold the landing for two seconds with your knees over your toes.
Next is Snap-down landing.
Back to Snap-down landing.
